lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs' skid has become a weekly ritual, and Saturday supplied the cruelest script yet. Columbus scored twice in 52 seconds late in the third period to erase Toronto's lead and win 4-3 - Matthew Knies, returning to Scotiabank Arena after his trade, tied it before Zach Werenski finished the comeback. The ovation for Knies turned sour quickly. Toronto is now 8-14, 13th in the Eastern Conference, 14 points behind, and riding a nine-game losing streak - four defeats in a row, including identical 4-3 losses to the Blue Jackets and Kings. William Nylander's costly clearing attempt became the pivot, while Anthony Stolarz could not hold the late advantage. No injury update changes the larger diagnosis: this team is leaking confidence and points. Monday's visit to the Islanders at 7:30 p.m. ET is less a reset than a test of whether Toronto can stop the slide before November buries the season.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The first meaningful decision of Toronto's winter was also its clearest warning: sentiment has no roster spot. The Blue Jays non-tendered Davis Schneider, cutting loose a fan favorite rather than pay his projected $1.3 million arbitration salary after a rough 2026. That move creates space, but it also exposes the assignment ahead - this club needs more outfield athleticism and more dependable offense, not another patchwork bench. The season is over, and the final points total was -2.0; now the accounting begins. Toronto tendered contracts to its other seven arbitration-eligible players, including Ernie Clement, Nathan Lukes and reliever Louis Varland, while Bowden Francis' Tommy John recovery complicates the pitching picture. The early market offers names such as Trevor Larnach, and bigger ambitions may point toward Randy Arozarena or Tarik Skubal. Watch the next ten days: Toronto must turn Schneider's vacancy into a genuine upgrade before the lockout turns urgency into paralysis.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors beat the Pistons 105-102, moving to 6-10 on the season. They sit 4th in atlantic division, and the standings race sharpens a little every night. Before that, the club lost to the Wizards 99-103. There is runway left in the schedule, and the work on rotations and matchups matters as much as the scoreboard. Next up: vs. Bucks on Mon 11/23 at 7:30 PM ET. Around the NBA, the offseason machinery is already whirring - front offices are mapping out draft boards, free-agent target lists are being quietly circulated, and cap projections are being stress-tested against every conceivable scenario. For the Toronto Raptors, the conversation centers on which direction the rebuild takes next and whether the draft lottery delivers the kind of franchise-altering talent that can accelerate the timeline.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders have finally found a pulse, but the standings leave no room for sentimentality. Washington is 3-5-1, sitting second in the NFC East and two games behind, with a one-game winning streak built on a 24-21 victory over the Giants 10 days ago. The immediate concern is the injury report: Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White, center Lucas Patrick and cornerback Amik Robertson are all questionable for Monday night against Cincinnati. Croskey-Merritt completed a full week of practice while working back from a groin injury, but White's heel kept him out Saturday, leaving a backfield that could change shape before kickoff. Robertson's late-practice ankle injury is just as unsettling against a Bengals offense capable of exploiting thin coverage. Jonathan Allen's return to Washington adds old emotion to a game already heavy with consequence. Monday's 8:15 p.m. meeting with Cincinnati is the test: protect the quarterback, stabilize the running game and turn a modest streak into a climb.
